items.hook: World War I: Start of the Battle of Mont Saint-Quentin, a successful assault by the Australian Corps during the Hundred Days Offensive.
items.body: World War I, or the First World War, also known as the Great War, was a global conflict between two coalitions: the Allies and the Central Powers. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: A LAPA Boeing 737-200 crashes during takeoff from Jorge Newbury Airport in Buenos Aires, killing 65, including two on the ground.
items.body: Líneas Aéreas Privadas Argentinas, more commonly known by the acronym LAPA, was an airline based in Buenos Aires, Argentina. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: The Black Garden review – haunting study of growing up in war-torn Nagorno-Karabakh
items.body:
Alexis Pazoumian’s documentary follows Samvel and Avo, two preteen boys whose lives will be unavoidably scarred by brutal conflict

After the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991, a decades-long territorial dispute exploded in the region

items.hook: K-PAX is a 2001 American science fiction mystery film starring Kevin Spacey as a psychiatric patient who claims to be an alien from the planet K-PAX and Jeff Bridges as the doctor who investigates his case.
items.body: It also stars Alfre Woodard and Mary McCormack. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: The Future Starts With Us by Gordon Brown review – the ex-PM’s recipe for beating populism
items.body:
Global crises are tightly linked to how we treat each other at the local level, argues this optimistic book

In times of crisis, there is one person to whom the left still turns for guidance.

items.hook: The Discovery of Heaven is a 1992 novel by Dutch writer Harry Mulisch.
items.body: It is considered Mulisch's masterpiece and was voted best book in the Dutch language in a 2007 poll among the readers of NRC Handelsblad. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: The 2005 Al-Aaimmah bridge stampede in Baghdad kills 953 people.
items.body: The Al-Aimmah Bridge disaster occurred on August 31, 2005 when 965 people died following a panic, and subsequent crowd crush, on the Al-Aaimmah Bridge, which crosses the Tigris river in the Iraqi capital of Baghdad. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: King Haakon V moves the capital of Norway from Bergen to Oslo.
items.body: Haakon V Magnusson was King of Norway from 1299 until 1319. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: Should we all be taking low doses of lithium to prevent Alzheimer’s?
items.body: Animal studies have shown that lithium orotate could help stave off dementia, and a human trial is about to start to see if the effects hold. Columnist Alice Klein takes a look at the benefits and downsides of lithium

items.hook: Switzy by Emma Cline review – this Booker-listed account of a man’s last days is profoundly moving
items.body:
Struggling with Alzheimer’s, the central character sets out on his final journey to a euthanasia clinic

The word “Alzheimer’s” never appears in Switzy, Emma Cline’s third novel, which arrives pre-endorsed as a Booker prize longlist

items.hook: Bel review – the powerful life force and haunting absence of a traumatised singer-songwriter
items.body:

items.hook: The Howling III: Echoes is a 1985 horror novel by the American author Gary Brandner.
items.body: It is the third and final entry in his Howling series of novels. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: Hints of fiery finale for last ever episode of River City
items.body: The Scottish soap opera, based in the fictional Glasgow district of Shieldinch, is coming to an end after 24 years.

items.hook: Pennsylvania Central Airlines Trip 19 crashes near Lovettsville, Virginia. The CAB investigation of the accident is the first investigation to be conducted under the Bureau of Air Commerce act of 1938.
items.body: On August 31, 1940, Pennsylvania Central Airlines Flight 19, a new Douglas DC-3, was flying from Washington, D.C. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: Cracks is the third novel by South African author Sheila Kohler.
items.body: Published in 1999, it was chosen as one of the best books of the year by both Newsday and Library Journal. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: This actor was told he had Alzheimer's, now he's performing a one-man show
items.body: Peter Marinker is taking on one of Samuel Beckett's most famous plays alone on a London stage.

items.hook: Edvard Munch's famous painting, The Scream, stolen on August 22, 2004, is recovered in a raid by Norwegian police.
items.body: Edvard Munch was a Norwegian painter. The world is stranger than it lets on.
